info.name: P2P · Supplier Purchase Invoice (SPI)
info.description:
The SPI flow end to end: Stage 01 supplier and PO, Stage 02 items (3-way match), Stage 03 box packaging, Stage 04 put-away (office allocation AND the Zebra handheld), close, Zoho Books, payments and the evidence vault.

SETUP
  1. Set {{base_url}} and {{sticker_url}}.
  2. Run 00 · Auth → Login. It stores {{token}}.
  3. For folder 07 you also need {{device_token}} — add a device in folder 09, or copy the credential from Inventory → Scan Devices.

IDS FILL THEMSELVES. Test scripts store spi_id, box_id, putaway_id, task_id, warehouse_id, zone_id, rack_id and shelf_id as you go.

STAGE 04 ORDER
  Set storage type → Board → Locations (counts) → Locations (tree) → Assign
  then EITHER  Confirm manually (06)
  or           Send for Zebra verification (06) → scan it in 07
  and finally  Submit (10), which refuses while any box is unplaced.

TWO KINDS OF AUTH
  Folders 00–06, 08–13 use the user bearer {{token}}.
  Folder 07 uses X-Scan-Device: {{device_token}} and NO user token — the tenant comes off the device row.

item.name: 00 · Auth

request.description: Stores {{token}} for every other request in the collection.

item.description: Run this first. Everything else reads {{token}}.

request.description: Read only — nothing is locked or reserved. Two users with the form open both see the same number; whoever saves first keeps it.
Each line carries qty_open = po.quantity − everything already invoiced. The same service method backs the save-time guard, so the number shown is the number enforced.
Not an SPI route — the standalone flow picks a supplier directly and reuses PoLookupController.
What Stage 04 allocates against. wh_type holds 'own' or a third-party value; the own/3PL split is read from here and never stored on the invoice.
rack_mode is the fork Stage 04 opens on: 'rack' zones own racks and shelves, 'norack' zones hold boxes directly and ARE the location.
A shelf must belong to a rack in the zone being assigned, or assign refuses it.

Shelves hang off their RACK — there is no /inventory/shelves/options.

A shelf has no code column of its own: its code is the rack's code plus the level (RC-001-SH-05).
Returns the flat row plus `tabs` with the five counts. The counts are unfiltered on purpose — a tab must still show its total while another tab is selected.

One query, LEFT JOINs out to the PO and through it to the shipment and opportunity.

Also: type 'direct spi without po' to pull up every standalone invoice — no column holds that phrase.
Invoice + items + owns_zoho_bill + packing_summary in one call, so the detail screen makes one request rather than three.
The condensed header used by the stage screens.

THE FIRST WRITE OF THE FLOW. Opening the form writes nothing — the code is allocated here, inside the transaction, under a lock on the BRANCH row. The sequence is per branch, so a new branch starts again at 001.

purchase_order_id is null — the 'Without Purchase Order' flow. Nothing consumes PO quantity, and THIS invoice owns its own Zoho bill.

currency_code is required when document_type is international.
Draft or mapped only. Changing purchase_order_id after items exist is refused — it would orphan every mapped line.

The WHOLE grid saves at once — never row by row, or the header totals and the lines disagree between requests.

The SERVER computes taxable_amount, the GST split and line_total; the client never sends an amount. On an international invoice the four tax columns are written NULL, not 0 — 'does not apply' is a different fact from 'charged at zero rate'.

422 if qty_spi exceeds what is left on the PO line.
Preview only — nothing is reserved.

qty_packed is DERIVED — SUM(box_items.quantity) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Nothing is stored on the item.

QA case: pack 10, delete a box of 4, confirm pending reads 4 and not 0. A missing soft-delete filter makes a removed box still count as packed.
The row shape this stage's form posts back — ids, a raw flags array, invoice-item references. For the resolved read, use 'Packed boxes' below.

Box and contents in ONE payload — packed quantity is summed from the contents, so a box saved without them would read as empty.

box_code is allocated by the server, sequential WITHIN the invoice. Three SPIs packed at once never interleave.

Batch, expiry, serial and lot sit on the ITEM, not the box: one carton can hold two products from two batches.

Contents are replaced wholesale — a partial update would leave quantities from a product the user just removed.

The over-pack guard ignores THIS box's own current rows, or an edit could never keep its existing quantity.

Soft delete; the quantity goes back to pending. Returns `renumbered` — the boxes after it close the gap, EXCEPT any whose sticker is already printed.

Refused when the box is already put away.
Stamps sticker_printed_at and returns code_locked: true. From then on the box is never renumbered — the label is physically on a carton being scanned at put-away.

The 4x6in label as a PDF. Its QR carries the SIGNED STICKER URL — {{sticker_url}}/ps/CBC1.<tenant>.BOX.<id>.<nonce>.<sig> — so a phone that photographs it opens our server rather than being shown a bare string.

Stamps sticker_printed_at the first time.

Every packed box with its contents RESOLVED: the product named, the flags read from the master, the put-away location once it has one, the sticker and the attachments.

This is the READ Stage 04 Step 01 is built on.

item.name: 06 · Stage 04 — put-away allocation (office)

request.description: Only warehouse_id is stored. putaway_mode in the response is derived from the warehouse master: 'full' for our own warehouse (rack → shelf), 'summary' for a 3PL.

item.name: Board — every box, its status and step

request.description:
Step 01's left rail in ONE read: every box with its status (pending | draft | awaiting_scan | placed), its sub-step, its destination once assigned, and the counts behind the PLACED bar.

Driven from the BOXES, not the put-away rows — a box nobody has started has no put-away row at all, and that is exactly the box the operator is looking for.
Every put-away row of the invoice. Use this before Submit to see which boxes are still unplaced.

Without `mode`, only the two numbers the opening modal asks for:

  modes.rack   — shelves available in RACKED zones
  modes.norack — active zones that hold boxes directly

422 unless the invoice has a warehouse — run 'Set storage type' first.

ONE call serves both halves of the screen:

  recommended — the best spot, its score and the parts that make it up
  zones[]     — zone > rack > shelf, each with its fill, used_pct, used_pct_after and eligible counts

The recommendation is the TOP OF THE SAME ranked list the tree is built from, so the two cannot disagree.

Scoring: fit 45 · consolidate 20 · ergonomics 20 · grouping 15 · proximity 0 (dormant until zones carry a layout sequence). Fit rewards the TIGHTEST fit, not the emptiest shelf.

Every ineligible shelf carries a reason: inactive · in_use · no_cold_chain · no_hazardous · no_temp_control · temp_out_of_range · too_tall · full · over_weight · over_capacity.

exec: console.warn('no eligible shelf ·', r.data ? r.data.eligible + '/' + r.data.total : '');

item.name: Assign a location (the box becomes a DRAFT)

request.description:
Step 02's commit, and the first write of Stage 04. ONE transaction: locks the location, RESERVES its capacity, creates the put-away row, resyncs the shelf counters and writes the activity trail.

CAPACITY IS TAKEN HERE, not at confirmation — a Zebra task can sit open for hours and the shelf must not read as free meanwhile.

Call it AGAIN with a different shelf and it is the Change button: the previous hold is released first, logged as 'reassigned' with both addresses.

409 when another operator holds that location. 422 when the shelf is not on a rack in that zone, when rack_mode does not match, or when the box is already placed.

For a NO-RACK zone send mode=norack and omit rack_id and shelf_id.

Step 03, Option 02. `confirmed` is the finality tick from the dialog and must be accepted — send false and it is refused with 422.

Flips the occupancy reserved → occupied, stamps confirmed_at and verify_method=manual, and releases the lock.

THE SHELF COUNTERS DO NOT MOVE here: the space was taken at assign. What changes is who says the box is on the shelf.

Refused with 422 while a Zebra task is open on this box — cancel it first.

item.name: Send for Zebra verification — Option 01 (CREATES A TASK)

request.description:
Step 03, Option 01. Returns 201 with task_code ZT-YYYYMMDD-NNN, numbered per branch per day.

THE BOX STAYS UNPLACED: confirmed_at remains null, the row reads awaiting_scan, the capacity stays reserved, and the lock follows the task's deadline rather than the screen's idle timeout.

A second task on the same box is refused, and so is manual confirmation while this one is open.

item.description: Order: Set storage type → Board → Locations (counts) → Locations (tree) → Assign → then EITHER 'Confirm manually', OR 'Send for Zebra verification' and finish it in folder 07.

item.name: 07 · Stage 04 — Zebra handheld (device auth)
Device session — who am I, what is open

request.description:
The first call the handheld makes. Returns the device, whether a person has CLAIMED it, and the open task queue the scan page lists.

401 when the credential is unknown, 403 when the device is suspended or has no enrolled user.

scanned_value accepts every shape a scanner can produce: the signed URL, the bare key, the pipe form, 'SH:1', or a legacy bare box id. Case is normalised.

With no task_id the box's own open task is picked up. With one, a different box is refused by name — "Wrong box — this task wants B-002."

Refusals: already_placed · no_task · unknown_box · wrong_box · bad_signature · unreadable.

ANY level of the address is accepted — zone, rack or shelf — in any order. Scanning the SHELF ticks its rack and zone too, because a shelf cannot be anywhere but its own rack.

Only the deepest assigned level finishes the location. The response carries `chain` (each level with scanned true/false) and `next_level`.

The KIND is checked before the id: shelf 1, rack 1 and zone 1 all exist, so comparing ids alone would take a rack label as proof of standing at the shelf.

Three refusals in a row reset the task to the box.

item.name: Scan — a location with nothing due (lookup)

request.description:
Scanned with no task in hand and nothing due there, the same call answers the OTHER question: what is currently in this location. Boxes, weight used, free capacity — reserved rows included and marked 'on its way'.

When something IS due, it stages the location and waits for a box.
Everything the scan page draws: device, task, chain, box details, destination. Works on a FINISHED task too — a read never requires the task to still be open.

slot: box | shelf | zone.

Not normally needed — the scan that closes the pair completes the put-away by itself. Kept for a client that wants to acknowledge each half explicitly.

Normally never called: once both halves are scanned the put-away completes on its own, because the barcodes have already proved everything a button press could.

When it does run: occupancy reserved → occupied, put-away → placed with verify_method=scan, lock released, task → scanned.

422 until both halves are scanned. 409 when the location is no longer held for this box.

item.description:
Device-authenticated — send X-Scan-Device: {{device_token}}, NOT a user bearer token. The tenant is read off the device row, and the person who enrolled it authors every scan.

Flow: Session → Scan box → Scan location → done. Either order works.

item.name: Queue — every open task in the branch

request.description:
The floor's queue ACROSS invoices, open first, paginated. status: pending | scanned | cancelled | expired — omit it for everything.

Note the path: this one is not scoped to an invoice.

item.name: Tasks of one invoice (the awaiting banner)

request.description: The 'Awaiting Zebra confirmation' banner and its scan chips, with this invoice's awaiting / placed / cancelled / expired counts.

Where this box is up to: step, step_label, is_open, is_done, ready_to_complete, attempts_left and every timestamp.

Cheap enough for a screen to poll — about 1.4 KB, against 22 KB for the activity read below.

item.name: One task — activity (every scan, pass and fail)

request.description:
How the box got there, in order — and the ONLY place refusals survive.

On the task row a put-away that took four attempts and one wrong rack is indistinguishable from a clean one. The difference lives here.

Each row: event, ok, meta.reason, meta.value (the raw string scanned), actor, device_id. Plus counts {total, passed, failed}.

Closes the task and NOTHING else.

The occupancy stays RESERVED and the location stays LOCKED, because the screen reopens on the same shelf offering manual confirmation — letting the shelf go in between would hand it to somebody else mid-decision.

Works on a PARTLY SCANNED task. Refused once the task is scanned, cancelled or expired.

After cancelling, the SAME put-away id is confirmed by hand in folder 06.
The handheld allow-list for this client.
Returns the plaintext credential ONCE. Only its hash is stored, so it cannot be read back later.
Issues a new credential and invalidates the old one IMMEDIATELY. Any handheld holding the previous one stops working and must be enrolled again — and the old plaintext cannot be recovered.

item.name: Enroll — claim the device for a person

request.description:
Run ON the handheld, SIGNED IN. Whoever is signed in becomes the author of every put-away this device later confirms (scan_devices.enrolled_by).

Skip it and scans fall back to created_by — the admin who added the device row, not the person moving boxes.
Is this credential allowed to scan right now. Public and throttled — it is a guessing surface.
status: active | suspended | retired. A suspended device is told so by name when it tries to scan.
Removes it from the allow-list.

Sets status=mapped and stage_completed=4. This is the ONLY place stage_completed is written — nothing auto-advances the invoice when the last box is placed.

Refused while anything is UNPACKED: goods not in a box have no box code, so they cannot be scanned, racked or inspected.

Refused while anything is UNPLACED, naming the boxes and returning them in `unplaced`.
Soft delete. Before the invoice goes, every line gives its quantity BACK to the PO through the fulfilment ledger — skip that and the PO stays short forever with no trace why.
Only an invoice with NO purchase order creates its own bill — with a PO the bill already exists on the order and must not be created twice.\n\nCurrently returns 501: the bill call is not written yet.
When the invoice does NOT own the bill, the response names the PO that does — rather than an empty state that reads like a failed sync.
The payment history popup.

item.name: Record a payment against a request

request.description: Every document attached to the invoice and its boxes, grouped.
The same read on the purchase order.
